transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Michael Park (VP Eng, CedarTech), Sana Ahmed (Platform Lead), Luis Ortega (Security), Jules Kim (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on CedarTech's Dedicated needs: reserved GPU capacity, isolation requirements (VPC/on-prem consideration), burst strategy, scaling expectations, and security/KMS questions. Agreed to run a benchmark and share capacity planning spreadsheet + pricing.

Topics:
- Current stack and workloads (inference patterns, seq lengths, peak QPS)
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs (latency guarantees, cost, data isolation)
- Burst handling and autoscaling expectations
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 and network controls
- Next steps and benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes. small intro — I'm Alex Chen, AE at Redwood, with Priya our solutions eng.
[00:08] Michael: Hey Alex, thanks. Michael Park here, VP of Eng at CedarTech. we've got Sana, Luis and Jules with me.
[00:12] Sana: hi all.
[00:13] Luis: hey.
[00:15] Priya: great, thanks. quick agenda, want to understand your current inference footprint, what constraints you have, and whether Dedicated makes sense vs our hosted offering.
[00:23] Michael: sure, so high level — CedarTech runs document ingestion and semantic search across customer docs, also live triage chat for support. About 1.2M requests/day, avg sequence length ~600 tokens, but for some docs >2k. Peak traffic during end-of-month reports pushes QPS up about 8x for an hour.
[00:40] Jules: just to add, our models are mainly open weights right now, finetuned Llama variants, we run some reranking and embeddings on the side. Latency target for chat is sub 500ms p95.
[00:50] Alex: ok, that helps. when you say 1.2M requests/day, is that inference calls or API hits including embedding jobs?
[00:56] Jules: mix, roughly 70% chat/inference, 30% batch embeddings and rerank. embeddings are less latency sensitive.
[01:02] Priya: got it. couple of quick questions: how strict is your data isolation requirement — do you need a private control plane or is dedicated capacity in a shared control plane acceptable?
[01:12] Michael: we prefer full tenant isolation — VPC peering and dedicated capacity. eventually may want an on-prem option for regulated customers.
[01:20] Luis: and from security side we need KMS-integrated key management, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SAML SSO integration. SOC 2 is a baseline.
[01:30] Alex: totally reasonable. Dedicated supports VPC + private subnets, and we have Private option for a full customer-controlled control plane, on-prem package as well. we'll include that in the doc.
[01:39] Sana: questions on autoscaling — we want predictable baseline throughput with the ability to burst by, say, 2-3x for short windows. how does Redwood handle that with reserved GPUs? do you spin up more GPUs or allow burst on hosted spare capacity?
[01:52] Priya: good question. typically for Dedicated we provision a reserved pool sized for your baseline commit. for short bursts we offer configurable burst capacity — two modes: 1) burst within the Dedicated pool via warm standby nodes (faster but more expensive), or 2) route bursts to hosted capacity as overflow (cheaper but with looser SLOs). we can combine both.
[02:12] Michael: hmm, routing bursts to hosted sounds risky for us due to data residency — but maybe acceptable if payloads are redacted. how do you secure that path?
[02:20] Alex: if you don't want any cross-tenant routing, we can enable warm-standby bursting entirely within your Dedicated pool. that requires reserving some headroom or autoscaling that spins up nodes in your Dedicated cluster — there is a tradeoff on cost and time-to-scale. typical time to add new GPU nodes in Dedicated is 4 minutes depending on region and instance type.
[02:39] Jules: 4 minutes is long for live chat spikes, we need <2 minutes ideally. is there a warm KV cache or pre-warmed kernel option?
[02:47] Priya: yes, for latency-sensitive traffic we recommend two tactics: 1) pre-warmed worker blades for the fastest response (seconds), and 2) aggressive prefix/KV caching to reduce token generation work for common requests. the warm blades are more expensive because they sit ready.
[03:03] Michael: can you quantify cost delta? like if baseline is 10 GPUs and we keep 2 warm blades, how much more are we talking? ballpark numbers are fine.
[03:12] Alex: we'll send detailed pricing but very roughly warm capacity adds about 15-30% to dedicated reserved spend depending on GPU type. hosted overflow could be 20-40% cheaper but without guaranteed latency and with the data routing caveat.
[03:27] Luis: on encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? We require CMEK for model inputs at rest.
[03:33] Priya: yes we support KMS integrations and can use your KMS for stored artifacts; for in-transit and in-memory we use standard protections but HSM-based attestation for keys is possible in Private/on-prem deployments. will capture details in security doc.
[03:44] Sana: scale expectations — if we grow 4x in 12 months, what's the path? how easy is it to add more reserved GPUs?
[03:52] Priya: adding to Dedicated is straightforward — you can expand the reserved pool with a commit change, typically a one to two week lead time for capacity planning on large counts but smaller increments are faster. our autoscaler can handle vertical scaling of workers and you can add GPU types for different workloads.
[04:06] Michael: what's your recommended GPU mix for our workload? we have long context runs and medium batch embeddings.
[04:12] Priya: for long-context Llama variants, we typically recommend A800-style instances for cost-sensitive high-throughput, or A100 if you need max perf for shorter latencies. For long sequences >1k tokens, larger memory cards or multi-gpu sharding helps. I'll share a spreadsheet with options.
[04:27] Jules: any support for quantized models to save memory? we run 4-bit quantized finetunes sometimes.
[04:33] Priya: yes we support quantization-friendly runtimes — sometimes you get 2x memory improvements with modest accuracy delta.
[04:42] Luis: audit logs — can we stream audit logs to our SIEM and have per-token cost telemetry?
[04:48] Alex: yes we have per-request tracing and cost breakdowns. Audit logs can be forwarded via secure syslog or S3 delivery to your enclave. we'll include sample retention and formats.
[04:59] Michael: ok good. another item — network topology: we need VPC peering and ability to route through our firewall for PCI segments.
[05:06] Priya: VPC peering is supported, and we can place nodes inside dedicated subnets with NAT/firewall rules in front. For on-prem we offer an appliance that sits behind your firewall.
[05:16] Sana: about canary and rollout controls — we need A/B testing and automatic fallback if quality drops. are those in the Dedicated offering?
[05:24] Alex: yes rollout controls are part of the platform — canary, traffic-split, automatic fallbacks to safe model variants. We'll also hook up quality monitoring to your eval sets if you want regression alerts.
[05:36] Jules: speaking of evals, we have prompt sets we run nightly. can Redwood run those during benchmarks to give us a quality/cost tradeoff report?
[05:43] Priya: absolutely, we can run your eval prompts on candidate model/quantization combos and return latency/quality/cost matrix. helps pick the right quantization and GPU mix.
[05:52] Michael: what about SLA and uptime? if we run customer-facing chat, we need 99.9+ uptime and p95 latency guarantees.
[05:59] Alex: Dedicated comes with SLA tiers; 99.9 is achievable with committed capacity and configured redundancy. We'll include service targets in the SOW.
[06:08] Luis: any compliance packages? we have some customers requiring FedRAMP-ish controls.
[06:12] Alex: we have SOC 2 and ISO docs; for higher bar like FedRAMP we can discuss an enterprise compliance package and Private/on-prem install.
[06:20] Sana: timeline — we're looking to pilot in Q1, with production by mid-Q2 next year. is that feasible?
[06:26] Priya: yes pilot in Q1 is reasonable. we'll need traffic logs to size baseline and a short benchmark run.
[06:32] Michael: ok next steps?
[06:34] Alex: recap — Alex will send pricing and SLO examples, Priya will share capacity planning spreadsheet and GPU recommendations, we'll schedule a benchmark (SE-led) week of 2026-11-16, CedarTech to provide traffic profile and security questionnaire answers.
[06:48] Michael: yep that sounds right. Jules will pull logs.
[06:50] Jules: yep will do.
[06:51] Luis: I'll get security Qs answered.
[06:53] Alex: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark and attach the docs.
[06:58] Michael: thanks Alex, Priya. Appreciate it.
[07:00] Alex: thanks all, bye.

Notes on transcription quality: Several proper nouns were auto-transcribed (e.g., GPU families) and may be slightly off. There were brief crosstalk segments.

Referenced artifacts/links: Redwood Dedicated pricing deck (link sent post-call), Capacity planning spreadsheet (to be shared), Security questionnaire (link), Benchmark run plan (to be scheduled).
